nodes.title: How do resource constraints shape neural codes?
nodes.statement: Which response statistics and learning routes preserve useful representations under explicit activity or metabolic constraints?
scope: Organising question, not a validated claim

nodes.title: Expected-cost maximum entropy yields a Gibbs frontier
nodes.statement: For the specified response space and expected-cost constraint, entropy-maximising response laws form a Gibbs family along the active Pareto frontier.
nodes.independent_unit: Formal optimisation problem under stated assumptions
background: Neural response entropy is optimised subject to an expected-cost budget.

evidence.design: Formal optimisation of response entropy under normalisation and expected-cost constraints.
evidence.sample: Admissible response distributions under the stated cost model.
evidence.independent_units: The formal theorem and its assumptions.
evidence.result: The optimiser has Gibbs form and the frontier slope is the marginal entropy return per unit cost.
evidence.uncertainty: The result is conditional on the stated response space and cost function; CV is only a coordinate on specified injective branches.

non_claims: Does not show that every empirical neural response distribution is Gibbs.
Does not make CV a global or unique efficiency coordinate.
falsification: A valid counterexample satisfies the formal assumptions but has a non-Gibbs entropy maximiser.
nodes.interpretation: The frontier can organise positive and negative empirical tests without requiring every system to realise the same response law.

nodes.title: Lifetime CV tracks calibrated information per cost in macaque V1
nodes.statement: Across five macaque V1 sessions from three animals, firing-rate-controlled lifetime CV tracked measured stimulus information per calibrated cost.
nodes.independent_unit: Animal/session hierarchy; confirm exact inferential unit before deposit
background: The Gibbs frontier motivates CV as a branch-local coordinate rather than a universal efficiency measure.

evidence.design: Within-session association between lifetime CV and direct-method stimulus information per calibrated cost after firing-rate control.
evidence.sample: Five macaque V1 sessions from three animals.
evidence.independent_units: Sessions nested within animals; author must confirm the deposited inferential unit.
evidence.analysis: Firing-rate-controlled association and independent-half decoder diagnostics.
evidence.result: Lifetime CV tracked measured stimulus information per calibrated cost in every analysed session.
evidence.uncertainty: Conventional tuning metrics absorb incremental decoder contribution; CV is a compact correlate rather than a unique biomarker.

non_claims: Does not establish that CV uniquely causes efficient coding.
Does not establish universal transfer beyond the analysed V1 sessions.
falsification: The association disappears under the prespecified firing-rate-controlled reanalysis.
alternatives: Stimulus-tuning dispersion captured by conventional tuning measures may account for the association.
nodes.interpretation: CV may serve as a compact branch-local readout of information-cost operating position.

nodes.title: Negative binomial wins the held-out response-law comparison
nodes.statement: In native-count, shared-shape leave-one-session-out comparisons, negative-binomial models had the highest predictive density in every analysed fold.

evidence.design: Shared-shape candidate distributions were fit without the held-out session and scored on its native counts.
evidence.sample: Spontaneous and driven V1 sessions described in the manuscript.
evidence.analysis: Held-out predictive-density comparison among power-cost, lognormal and negative-binomial models.
evidence.result: Negative binomial achieved the highest predictive density in every fold.
evidence.uncertainty: This tests the candidate response law, not the existence of the objective-space Pareto frontier.

non_claims: Does not invalidate the entropy-cost frontier.
Does not establish negative binomial as a universal neural response law.
falsification: A correctly reproduced fold gives another candidate higher held-out predictive density.

nodes.title: PopCV regularisation restructures the active set in tested SDTs
nodes.statement: In the tested static-image SDT settings, population-CV regularisation reduced evaluation CV, increased effectively silent coordinates, and preserved or improved task accuracy.
nodes.independent_unit: Training seed within locked architecture-dataset protocol

evidence.design: Seeded comparison of baseline and population-CV regularised SDT training under the released protocol.
evidence.analysis: Paired accuracy, mean firing rate, evaluation PopFR-CV and effectively silent-coordinate summaries.
evidence.result: Evaluation CV decreased while effectively silent coordinates expanded, with preserved or improved task accuracy in the headline tested settings.
evidence.uncertainty: The released evidence does not establish universal superiority or a unique causal mechanism.

non_claims: Does not establish universal superiority to mean-firing-rate penalties.
Does not establish direct hardware energy savings.
Does not transfer unchanged to every SNN architecture.
falsification: Released seed-matched aggregation fails to reproduce the stated operating-point differences.
alternatives: The operating point may depend on architecture-specific surrogate-gradient geometry.
nodes.interpretation: Accessible optimisation routes can matter as much as an objective's unconstrained extremum.

nodes.title: Delayed onset prevents the observed early-silencing collapse
nodes.statement: Delayed-onset regularisation prevented the only no-warmup collapse observed in the six tested loss–dataset–coefficient cells without changing the selected operating point.
nodes.independent_unit: Tested loss–dataset–coefficient cell and seed protocol

evidence.design: Compare regularisation from training start against delayed onset across six selected cells.
evidence.sample: Six loss, dataset and coefficient cells in the manuscript ablation.
evidence.independent_units: Protocol cells and their training seeds.
evidence.analysis: Collapse incidence and final operating-point comparison.
evidence.result: One no-warmup cell collapsed and delayed onset prevented that observed collapse without changing the selected final operating point.
evidence.uncertainty: This is a safety margin for the tested case, not a universal rescue theorem.

non_claims: Does not show that delayed onset is necessary in every run.
Does not guarantee rescue from every training failure.
falsification: The specified collapsed configuration still collapses under the reproduced delayed-onset protocol.

nodes.title: Cross-species auditory capacity–reliability–accuracy matrix
nodes.statement: A frozen matched-stimulus protocol will vary evidence-constrained auditory and circuit parameters while holding stimulus, network size, readout, split and training budget fixed.
non_claims: No numerical receiver effect is currently claimed.
No reproducible Pareto trade-off is claimed before the matrix passes its gates.

nodes.title: Degree-preserving wiring minimisation reconstructs connectome topology
nodes.statement: The thesis reports that degree-preserving wiring-cost minimisation reconstructed topology more accurately than clustering-, modularity- or efficiency-targeting controls across five species.
nodes.independent_unit: Species connectome; exact datasets and statistics require chapter-level mapping
non_claims: The thesis abstract is not sufficient evidence for deposit.
Does not establish wiring cost as the only developmental objective.

nodes.title: A self-evolving SNN spans salt-and-pepper to pinwheel organisation
nodes.statement: The thesis reports that retinotopic geometry with Hebbian-homeostatic plasticity reproduced a range of V1 organisations from salt-and-pepper layouts to pinwheel maps.
nodes.independent_unit: Simulation condition; exact seeds and comparison criteria require mapping
non_claims: Does not establish the biological developmental mechanism.
Requires the original project artifacts before deposit.

nodes.title: Does learning history remain visible at matched current state?
nodes.statement: When gate and input are held fixed, can prior learning leave a measurable trace in effective recurrent interactions?
scope: Organising question, not a validated claim

nodes.title: Matched-current recurrent interactions retain training history
nodes.statement: In the tested SG-EAP matched-current protocol, different training histories left different recurrent-interaction readouts under the same final gate and input probe.
nodes.independent_unit: Paired model initialisation within the matched-current cohort protocol

evidence.design: Low-only, high-only, high-to-low and low-to-high histories were compared after common final-state exposure under the same gate and input probe.
evidence.sample: Four history cohorts with paired initialisations in the rebuttal experiment package.
evidence.analysis: Comparison of final interaction-correlation slopes under matched current conditions.
evidence.result: Different histories left different effective recurrent-interaction readouts at the matched probe.
evidence.uncertainty: This is an existence result in the tested correlated-input setting, not universal input generality.

non_claims: Does not show that every adaptive circuit retains the same history trace.
Does not establish a biological history effect in V1.
falsification: Paired cohorts become indistinguishable under the prespecified matched-current analysis.
alternatives: Optimizer state and other hidden adaptive variables may contribute to the observed trace.
nodes.interpretation: Matched-current probes separate learning history from immediate drive more directly than endpoint sign comparisons.

nodes.title: Matched N=100 runs share one switching order
nodes.statement: Under the matched N=100 SG-EAP protocol, cooperation-to-competition crossed before competition-to-cooperation in all 27 tested runs.
scope: Three batches and three initialisations per family

evidence.design: Both transition directions used matched budgets and crossing definitions across three tested input families.
evidence.sample: Twenty-seven runs formed by three input families, three input batches and three model initialisations.
evidence.analysis: Prespecified crossing-time comparison with censoring retained.
evidence.result: Cooperation-to-competition crossed first in 27 of 27 tested N=100 runs.
evidence.uncertainty: Timing magnitude depends on optimizer state and the N=100 ordering was unresolved at N=1000 because one direction was right-censored.

non_claims: Does not establish a universal timing ratio.
Does not establish scale invariance.
Does not establish SG-EAP uniqueness.
falsification: A valid run under the frozen matched N=100 protocol yields the reverse crossing order.
alternatives: A state-gated Oja-style comparator can produce the same directional asymmetry.
nodes.interpretation: The direction is protocol-reliable in the tested N=100 setting while its magnitude and mechanism remain bounded.

nodes.title: Which activity observables identify circuit dynamics?
nodes.statement: Do covariance scaling and near-real fitted dynamics uniquely imply symmetric, critically normalised recurrent structure?

nodes.title: A covariance exponent maps to a parameter swath
nodes.statement: In the analysed linear model, each fixed covariance power-law exponent in the reported cortical range occurs along an iso-exponent curve over reciprocity and spectral abscissa rather than at one symmetric-critical point.
nodes.independent_unit: Analytic parameter pair and reproduced numerical grid

evidence.design: Evaluate the covariance exponent over reciprocity and effective spectral abscissa.
evidence.sample: Parameter grid covering the reported cortical and brain-wide exponent range.
evidence.independent_units: Parameter settings supported by the analytic relation.
evidence.analysis: Lyapunov covariance analysis and iso-exponent tracing.
evidence.result: Fixed exponents occur along curves and the reported range maps to a parameter swath.
evidence.uncertainty: The conclusion is an identifiability counterexample within the analysed model class.

non_claims: Does not show that cortical dynamics are non-critical.
Does not identify the true biological reciprocity.
falsification: Within the stated model, the exponent uniquely determines reciprocity and spectral abscissa.

nodes.title: Near-real fitted eigenvalues do not imply symmetry
nodes.statement: A non-symmetric non-normal similarity transform of a symmetric operator can preserve its real eigenvalues and zero DMD rotation while passing the analysed covariance and memory diagnostics.
scope: Analysed DMD, covariance and memory diagnostics

evidence.design: Construct A = T S T^-1 from a symmetric parent S and compare observables.
evidence.sample: Constructed parent and transformed operator pairs.
evidence.analysis: Spectrum, DMD rotation, covariance, rank-timescale and scaled memory comparisons.
evidence.result: The non-normal operator preserves the tested real-spectrum observables despite lacking symmetry.
evidence.uncertainty: This is an existence counterexample, not an estimate of biological non-normality.

non_claims: Does not claim that the measured biological operator is the constructed transform.
Does not rule out symmetric dynamics by itself.
falsification: The constructed non-normal operator fails one of the stated equal-observable checks under exact reproduction.

nodes.title: FlyWire reciprocity does not determine the two fitted observables
nodes.statement: Across the tested FlyWire graph controls and operating points, neither the DMD spectrum nor the covariance exponent was determined by known structural reciprocity alone.

evidence.design: Vary structural reciprocity with degree-preserving graph controls while retaining in/out degree, weight multiset and Dale sign.
evidence.sample: Original, symmetrised and degree-preserving FlyWire graph controls across tested operating points.
evidence.result: The two fitted observables were not determined by known reciprocity alone across tested conditions.
evidence.uncertainty: The tested model and controls do not exhaust all connectome statistics or operating regimes.

non_claims: Does not establish that reciprocity is functionally irrelevant.
Does not identify the biological circuit mechanism.
falsification: Under the frozen controls, the observables become a unique function of reciprocity alone.
alternatives: Other structural features or operating-point variables may determine the observables.
nodes.interpretation: Known structural ground truth can expose non-uniqueness that activity-only fitting cannot resolve.

nodes.title: Reciprocity–stability direction depends on normalisation
nodes.statement: In the audited ESN confirmation, higher reciprocity increased post-perturbation stability under maximum-real normalisation, while the trend was absent under paired maximum-modulus normalisation.
nodes.independent_unit: Seeded recurrent matrix within a matched-normalisation protocol
non_claims: Does not establish universal behavioural robustness.
Does not establish monotonic noisy-integration accuracy.
not_tested: Final manuscript evidence ledger and exact uncertainty mapping
alternatives: Spectral normalisation changes the effective dynamical comparison.

nodes.title: What is readable now, and what transfers across episodes?
nodes.statement: Do anatomical systems differ in immediate task-variable readout and in the temporal scope over which slow associations generalise?

nodes.title: Thalamic and midbrain populations show stronger immediate readout
nodes.statement: In the frozen IBL cohort, thalamic and midbrain populations showed stronger current-stimulus and choice/action-linked readout than hippocampal formation after the stated nuisance and population controls.
scope: Matched firing rate, dimensionality and neuron-count controls

evidence.design: Compare stimulus and choice/action-linked balanced readout across systems with correlated-label balancing and population controls.
evidence.sample: Frozen cohort of 51 sessions from 30 mice and seven laboratories.
evidence.independent_units: Mice, with repeated sessions collapsed for inference.
evidence.analysis: Balanced-accuracy contrasts, nuisance balancing, cross-subject matching and neuron-count subsampling.
evidence.result: Thalamic/midbrain populations showed stronger immediate readout than hippocampal formation; zero-contrast choice remained readable in hippocampus.
evidence.uncertainty: Choice/action labels in the mixed task window do not isolate abstract choice from movement; fine relay localisation remains exploratory.

non_claims: Does not imply global hippocampal disengagement.
Does not isolate abstract choice from movement in the mixed task window.
Does not exhaust the full IBL release.
falsification: The prespecified mouse-level contrasts no longer show the reported system difference under the stated controls.
alternatives: Residual task and movement covariation may contribute to choice/action-linked readout.
nodes.interpretation: Brain systems may differ in task-variable allocation rather than expressing a uniform hierarchy of the same information.

nodes.title: Block decoding does not transfer across held-out episodes
nodes.statement: In the analysed IBL task, probability-block labels were decodable with random trial folds but failed to generalise when complete block episodes were held out.

evidence.design: Compare conventional random trial cross-validation with validation that holds out complete block episodes.
evidence.sample: Eligible sessions and mice in the frozen 51-session cohort.
evidence.analysis: Balanced decoding with grouped episode transfer and whole-block permutation diagnostics.
evidence.result: Random-fold block labels were decodable, but the association did not generalise across held-out episodes.
evidence.uncertainty: Failure to transfer supports a temporal-scope boundary; it does not prove the absence of all task-state representations.

non_claims: Does not show that task state is absent from neural activity.
Does not invalidate within-episode block decoding.
falsification: A leakage-free reproduction shows reliable transfer to complete held-out episodes.
not_tested: Other definitions of latent task state
alternatives: Random-fold decoding may exploit episode-specific temporal associations.
nodes.interpretation: Validation split defines the temporal scope of what a decoder result can support.

nodes.title: A passive VISam/ACC model predicts mild sublinear integration
nodes.statement: The collaboration model predicts mildly sublinear simultaneous VISam/ACC integration under its fitted passive multi-compartment assumptions.
non_claims: Does not establish the in vivo nonlinear coefficient.
Does not use the post-250 ms preprocessing artifact.
